tools.name: load_device
tools.description: Load a stock device or User Library preset onto a track. Specify either path OR part_type, not both. The `path` argument accepts (a) classic browser paths like "Instruments/Operator" for stock devices, or (b) `query:` URIs from find_instruments_by_tag for user-tagged presets. NOTE: part_type=Bd/Snare/HiHat/Perc resolves to the bare "Instruments/Drum Rack", which loads empty (no samples). For drums to be audible, follow up with browse_devices "Drums" and load_device on a kit preset (.adg). Tonal part_types (Bass/Pad/Chord/etc.) load synths that sound by default.

parameters.name: track_id
parameters.description: Track number (1-based: 1, 2, … or 'first', 'second', …)

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Browser path (e.g. "Instruments/Operator") OR a query: URI from find_instruments_by_tag.

parameters.name: part_type
parameters.description: PartType shorthand; resolves through defaults.instruments

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: Insert position in device chain (1-based: 1 = first slot; omit to append at the end)

tools.name: browse_devices
tools.description: List immediate children of a Live browser path. Reads the Vibrai instrument-browser snapshot (written by the Vibrai Live remote script via SP9) in-process — no live Ableton connection required. Empty path returns the snapshot's top-level folders. Examples: 'Drums' (drum kit presets), 'Instruments/Operator' (Operator presets), 'Packs/<PackName>' (pack contents), 'User Library' (user-saved presets). Returns an empty list when the snapshot is missing — run install_vibrai_remote_script and refresh in Live.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Browser path string; empty = top-level snapshot folders.

tools.name: delete_device
tools.description: Remove a device from a track's top-level device chain by index. v1 scope: top-level chain only — nested racks (Drum Rack pads, Instrument Rack chains) are not addressable through this call. The device is gone immediately; there is no undo. Use list_devices to discover indices.

parameters.name: track_id
parameters.description: Track number (1-based: 1, 2, … or 'first', 'second', …)

parameters.name: device_index
parameters.description: Device chain position (1-based: 1 = first device in the chain)

tools.name: list_devices
tools.description: List devices currently loaded on a track in chain order. Returns each device's index, id, name, and class info — pass deviceId to list_automation_params / get_automation / write_automation.

parameters.name: track_id
parameters.description: Track number (1-based: 1, 2, … or 'first', 'second', …)

tools.name: get_default_instrument
tools.description: Return the resolved browser path for a part-type (defaults.instruments override or built-in).

parameters.name: part_type
parameters.description: PartType to resolve

tools.name: load_default_instruments
tools.description: Load each MIDI part's default instrument from a .vibrai project onto its track, so the rendered song is audible. Tonal parts get their resolved synth (defaults.instruments override or built-in); drum parts get a stock kit (.adg) auto-picked from the browser snapshot, falling back to an empty Drum Rack + warning when none is available. Idempotent: a track that already has a device is skipped. Run this after `generate` (or pass with_instruments=true to generate).

parameters.name: project_path
parameters.description: Path to the .vibrai file (defaults to Untitled.vibrai in CWD when omitted)

options.description: Pattern set to use. Only 'default' is supported.

commands.name: instrument refresh
commands.description: Rescan the browser snapshot via the Vibrai Live remote script

tools.name: find_instruments_by_tag
tools.description: Find user presets tagged 'vibrai:<suffix>'. Returns all matches: their browser URI (pass as load_device 'path'), display name, browser path, and the recognized/extra tag buckets. Empty array if no matches or no cache file. Tags are populated by the Vibrai Live remote script — see install_vibrai_remote_script.

parameters.name: suffix
parameters.description: Tag suffix to match (e.g. 'bass' for vibrai:bass). Case-insensitive.

parameters.name: include_extra
parameters.description: If true, also matches unrecognized 'extra' tag suffixes. Default false.

tools.name: refresh_instrument_tags
tools.description: Ask the Vibrai Live remote script to rescan the browser. Touches the trigger file and waits up to 30 seconds for the browser snapshot to be rewritten. Returns the new scanned_at + item_count, or INSTRUMENT_TAG_SCRIPT_NOT_RUNNING if the script doesn't respond. If you get the not-running error, run install_vibrai_remote_script and make sure Vibrai is enabled in Live's Preferences → Link/Tempo/MIDI → Control Surface. CLI: `vibrai instrument refresh`.

tools.name: list_browser_items
tools.description: List items from the Vibrai browser snapshot, optionally filtered by name substring, path substring, path prefix, kind, or tagged state. The snapshot is written by the Vibrai Live remote script; the user tags items via tag_instrument. Returns up to `limit` results starting at `offset` (for pagination).

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match against item name. Null/empty = all.

parameters.name: path_contains
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match against the full browser path (e.g. 'Basses' matches any item under a folder containing that word). Null = all.

parameters.name: path_prefix
parameters.description: Only return items whose browser path starts with this prefix (case-insensitive), e.g. 'Packs/F9 GALAXY'. Null = all.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Filter by kind: 'preset', 'device', 'rack'. Null = all kinds.

parameters.name: tagged
parameters.description: If true, only items with at least one user tag; if false, only untagged; null = both.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of qualifying results to skip before returning (for pagination). Default 0.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max results to return (default 50).

tools.name: show_instrument
tools.description: Show one browser item plus any user tags applied to it. Accepts an exact uri (contains ':' and '#') or a name substring; case-insensitive. Errors: INSTRUMENT_NOT_FOUND, MULTIPLE_MATCHES.

parameters.name: uri_or_search
parameters.description: Browser URI (exact match) or name substring (case-insensitive, single match required).

tools.name: tag_instrument
tools.description: Apply a Vibrai PartType tag to a browser item. Accepts an exact uri or a name substring (single match). Atomically updates instrument-tags.json. Errors: INSTRUMENT_NOT_FOUND, MULTIPLE_MATCHES, INVALID_PART_TYPE.

parameters.name: uri_or_search
parameters.description: Browser URI (exact) or name substring (case-insensitive, single match).

parameters.name: part_type
parameters.description: PartType to apply (case-insensitive). E.g. 'bass', 'pad', 'lead'.

tools.name: untag_instrument
tools.description: Remove a Vibrai PartType tag from a browser item. If the item ends with no tags at all (recognized + extra both empty), the record is dropped from the tag store. Errors: INSTRUMENT_NOT_FOUND, MULTIPLE_MATCHES, INVALID_PART_TYPE.

parameters.name: uri_or_search
parameters.description: Browser URI (exact) or name substring (case-insensitive, single match).

parameters.name: part_type
parameters.description: PartType to remove (case-insensitive).

tools.name: suggest_tags_from_folders
tools.description: Scan the browser snapshot and infer PartType tags from folder names. Returns suggestions only — call tag_instrument to apply them. Use 'prefix' to scope to a single pack (e.g. 'Packs/F9 GALAXY'). The default pattern set maps common folder names (Basses→Bass, Kicks→Bd, Pads→Pad, etc.) to PartTypes. Does not mutate any state.

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description: Browser path prefix to restrict the scan (e.g. 'Packs/F9 GALAXY'). Null/empty = entire snapshot.

parameters.name: pattern_set
parameters.description: Pattern set name. Only 'default' is supported. Null = default.

tools.name: apply_automation_template
tools.description: Author a composition-level automation slot on the .vibrai project's arrangement template. The slot is a symbolic key resolved through AutomationTargetMap (see list_automation_slots for the vocabulary per PartType). Slots fall into two families: bare-synth slots (synth_cutoff, synth_resonance, synth_volume) target a parameter on device 0 by LOM name; rack-macro slots (cutoff, resonance, macro_1..macro_16) target a macro on the first Instrument Rack on the chain, resolved at bounce-time. The project is loaded, mutated, validated, and saved. Idempotent on (sectionId, partId, slot). Use "all" in sections to apply to every section. Set apply_to_live: true to also push the just-applied slots into the running Live set via the safe bouncer (Spec A's atomic-rollback contract applies per slot). The .vibrai file is updated first, then each applied (section, part, slot) tuple is resolved to a bouncer-shaped envelope and bounced onto the existing arrangement clip at the section's position. Slots whose section has no arrangement clip are skipped with status SkippedNoArrangementClip — Spec B is an iteration tool, not bootstrapping. Verify what landed via get_arrangement_envelopes_ledger. Default false preserves the file-only flow that callers depend on today.

parameters.description: Absolute filesystem path to the .vibrai file.

parameters.name: part_id
parameters.description: Canonical part id from project.Parts[].Id

parameters.name: slot
parameters.description: Symbolic slot key (e.g. "cutoff", "resonance", "macro_3", "synth_cutoff"). Use list_automation_slots to enumerate keys for a PartType.

parameters.name: curve
parameters.description: AutomationCurve enum: LinearUp | LinearDown | ExpUp | ExpDown

parameters.name: sections
parameters.description: Section ids to apply to, or the single literal "all" to apply to every section in project.Sections

parameters.name: apply_to_live
parameters.description: If true, also push the applied slots into the running Live set via the safe bouncer. Default false — file-only authoring. Requires an existing populated arrangement; slots whose section has no arrangement clip are skipped with a status. See recipe `apply_automation_template_live` for the iteration flow.

tools.name: list_automation_slots
tools.description: Enumerate the symbolic automation slots supported for a PartType. Returns a list of {slot_key, target_kind, target_details, description}. target_kind is "device_param" or "macro". Macro slots resolve at bounce-time; device_param slots resolve to a fixed (device_index, param_name) pair. Returns an empty list for PartTypes with no entries (e.g. Bd, Sd, Hh).

parameters.name: part_type
parameters.description: PartType enum value: Pad, Lead, Bass, Arp, Bd, Sd, Hh, Other

tools.name: bounce_arrangement_automation
tools.description: ADVANCED PRIMITIVE — for routine 'write automation into the arrangement,' prefer place_arrangement_clip with carry_envelopes:true. Bounces one or more envelopes into Live's arrangement view by snapshotting overlapping clips, deleting them, writing a merged scratch clip, then duplicating it back into place. The operation is atomic: on any failure the original clips are restored to their pre-call state. On rollback failure the call throws BounceRollbackPartialException with per-clip restore status. Note: success rewrites every overlapping clip, losing clip name/color metadata in the process. See recipe `write_arrangement_automation` for the canonical safe path.

parameters.name: track_id
parameters.description: Track number (1-based: 1, 2, … or 'first', 'second', …)

parameters.name: length_beats
parameters.description: Length of the bounce window in beats

parameters.name: envelopes
parameters.description: Array of envelope specs. Each entry has a discriminated Target (kind="device_param" or "macro") and EITHER points or curveSpec.

tools.name: get_arrangement_envelopes_ledger
tools.description: Read back the in-process ledger of envelopes committed to Live's arrangement view by bounce_arrangement_automation or place_arrangement_clip (carry_envelopes:true). Use this for programmatic verification — the LOM read-back path (get_arrangement_clip_envelopes) returns empty for clips that arrived via duplicate-to-arrangement. The ledger is in-process, bounded LRU (256 per track), and resets on MCP server restart. See recipe `verify_arrangement_writes` for the full verification flow.

features.description: Show CLI, M4L bridge, and Python bridge versions.

commands.name: version
commands.description: Show Vibrai CLI, M4L bridge, and Python bridge versions.

tools.name: get_version
tools.description: Get the running Vibrai.Mcp server version (assembly) and the M4L bridge version (package.json), plus a best-effort license block (status, features_enabled, days_remaining). Bridge version is best-effort: if the bridge is unreachable or times out, the response still includes the MCP version with a bridge_status indicating the failure.

features.title: Update
features.description: Check for and apply self-updates to the Vibrai CLI, Max-for-Live device, and Python remote script. Scope: CLI binary + M4L device + Python remote script only — the MCP server binary is managed by Claude Desktop's extension manager. Supports check-only, interactive/non-interactive apply, force reinstall, and rollback to the previously installed binary.

commands.name: update
commands.description: Check for and optionally apply the latest Vibrai release

options.name: --check
options.description: Only report whether an update is available; make no changes.

options.name: --yes
options.description: Apply without the confirmation prompt (required for non-interactive use).

options.name: --force
options.description: Reinstall the latest release even if already up to date.

options.name: --rollback
options.description: Restore the previously installed CLI binary from backup.

tools.name: update
tools.description: Check for and optionally install the latest Vibrai release. By default (apply=false) this only reports whether an update is available. Pass apply=true to download + verify (SHA-256) + swap the vibrai CLI binary and reinstall the Max-for-Live device + Python remote script (via the same installer as install_device / install_vibrai_remote_script). Scope: CLI binary + M4L + Python only — it does NOT update this MCP server binary, which is managed by Claude Desktop's extension manager. If Ableton Live is running during an apply, M4L/Python changes take effect after you restart Live. Returns the current/latest version, update_available, per-component status, and (on apply) the actions taken.

parameters.name: apply
parameters.description: Apply the update (download + swap + reinstall). Default false = check only.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: Reinstall even if already up to date (default false).

parameters.name: rollback
parameters.description: Roll back to the previously installed CLI binary (default false).
